newsitem.title: USA: Double Eagle sets Wyoming drilling.
newsitem.headline: Double Eagle sets Wyoming drilling.

text.p: Double Eagle Petroleum and Mining said Monday it plans to start drilling the Waltman 14-24 development well in May to test the Fort Union sands at 4,500 feet in the Waltman Field, Natrona County, Wyoming.

The company has a 28.6 percent working interest and will serve as operator for the Waltman 14-24. The drill site is one mile from Marathon Oil Co's Waltman 21-19 well, in which Double Eatle has a 14.3 percent working interest, that was drilled in January 1997 and is producing 1.5 million cubic feet of natural gas per day.
After the Waltman 14-24 test has been drilled, Double Eagle said, it will evaluate its plans for additional drilling on its leasehold in this area.

It said Texaco Inc plans to drill a 3,000-foot Frontier test by May 31 in the Washakie Basin of Fremont County, Wyoming, and is attempting to form a 2,400-acre unit which would include about 288 net acres owned by Double Eagle, resulting in an about 12 percent working interest. The exact size of the unit and Double Eagle's final working interest are expected to be determined by the end of April.

The company also said it agreed with Prima Oil & Gas Co and John Lockridge for Prima to serve as operator for a 15,000-foot Lance test to be drilled in the Madden Field of Wyoming, where Double Eagle owns 480 gross and 240 net acres. Double Eagle owns a 50 percent working interest in the Lance test-well drill site, it said.

The company will keep a 25 percent working interest and will farm out a 25 percent working interest to Lockridge for which Lockridge will pay all drilling and completion costs, with a 7.5 percent working interest to revert to Double Eagle after payout.

KCS Energy Inc is completing a well to the Lance Formation adjacent to the company's Madden Field acreage. The company and Prima Oil will select the location for their Lance test after the KCS well has been completed, Double Eagle said.

The company's Lance test will be a direct offset to both the KCS well and to four producing Lance wells within one mile operated by Louisiana Land and Exploration Co. Prima will serve as operator for the test, which is anticipated to be drilled in late 1997 or the first half of 1998.

Also in the general vicinity of the company's Madden Field acreage, about six miles away, LL&E has announced open hole log analysis of its Big Horn 4-36 step-out well drilled to 24,600 feet to the Madison Formation, and as a result, LL&E has increased its estimate of proved and probable recoverable natural gas reserves in the Madison reservoir.

Although Double Eagle has no current plans to pursue this formation, and any such plans would be extremely expensive, this information may indicate potential long-term future opportunities, the company said.
It also said chief executive Stephen H. Hollis exercised options to purchase 50,000 common shares at $0.875 per share in January. ((-- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610.))
